summary: Phase 4.2 of direct-route plan v2 attempted and BLOCKED (sanctioned outcome, not a sorry): iterating boxI_raise_step over the finite derivation tree to obtain a fully general boxI_lift is unsound without an as-yet-unestablished rank/unique-parent (rooted-forest) invariant on Graph -- confirmed via a concrete 3-cycle counterexample (x->a->b->x) that satisfies 'unique parent per target' yet forces two independent, non-coincident existential raises on the newly-discovered node. This invariant is the module docstring's own flagged 'item 1: the tree-shape invariant', not-yet-established work belonging to the main induction (Phase 5), genuinely out of Phase 4.2's single-file scope. Landed instead: boxI_lift_star, a sound generalization of Phase 4.1's boxI_raise_step from ONE raw-neighbour of x to a finite Finset of x's DIRECT raw-neighbours (both directions), chained via Finset.induction using cs5FCIncest_lift/cs5FCIncest_raise. Sorry-free, axiom-clean ([propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only). Does not close the full recursive cascade (grandchildren) or the boxI case itself. Scoped build green, no Preserved Asset regressed, cs5FCIncest unweakened.

blockers.what_failed: boxI_lift (fully general finite-tree cascade of boxI_raise_step) not provable as stated for an arbitrary finite Graph.
blockers.what_was_tried: Landed boxI_lift_star: a Finset.induction chaining cs5FCIncest_lift (F1, down edges R x n) / cs5FCIncest_raise (F2, up edges R n x) across ALL of x's DIRECT raw-neighbours simultaneously, holding x's target fixed at the original raise fact hwx. Sorry-free, build green, axiom-clean.
blockers.root_cause: cs5FCIncest has no 'raise one endpoint only, keep the other exact' conjunct, so raising x forces every raw-neighbour to move, and a neighbour with its OWN further neighbours forces a cascade. A fully general cascade needs the raw graph to be an acyclic, rank-graded rooted forest (a rank function ht : Label Atom -> Nat with R a b -> ht b = ht a + 1, PLUS unique-parent-per-target) to avoid simultaneous, generally non-coincident raise constraints on a newly-discovered node -- verified via a hand-constructed 3-cycle counterexample (x->a, a->b, b->x) that satisfies unique-parent-per-target alone but still creates the conflict. Graph (Syntax.lean:110) has no finiteness or acyclicity field; this invariant does not exist anywhere in the codebase yet.
blockers.what_is_needed: Establish (or thread through the Phase 5 main induction directly) a rank/depth + unique-parent invariant on the raw graph relation used at each boxI/diaE step, then redo the boxI_lift_star-style Finset cascade under that invariant to cover the full raw-connected component of x, not just direct neighbours.
blockers.verbatim_goal_text: Prove `boxI_lift` by finite induction over the derivation tree, invoking `boxI_raise_step` node-by-node (the raising, not any exact edge, accommodates `w' >= rho x`).

Do NOT retry Phase 4.2 open-endedly; do NOT attempt Phase 5 without first resolving this invariant gap, since Phase 5's boxI case needs the full boxI_lift, not just boxI_lift_star.

decisions_made: Did not attempt to force a fully general boxI_lift via an ad-hoc/unverified acyclicity assumption smuggled in without justification; instead constructed and verified a concrete counterexample (3-cycle) showing why 'unique parent' alone is insufficient, then scoped the landed lemma (boxI_lift_star) to exactly the sound sub-case (direct neighbours only), per the plan's zero-debt and blocked-honesty contract.

Used `classical` (providing Classical.propDecidable, hence DecidableEq (Label Atom) via typeclass resolution) once at the top of the tactic proof, before Finset.induction and Function.update -- this DOES resolve the DecidableEq obligation for a generic Atom type, contradicting the prior Phase 4.1 dispatch's 'dead_ends' note that Function.update fails without a directly-supplied DecidableEq instance. Correction: it works when `classical` precedes the Finset.induction/Function.update usage in the same tactic block scope.
dead_ends: Attempting to state boxI_lift for an arbitrary finite Graph.X (Set.Finite hypothesis only, no acyclicity): the 3-cycle x->a->b->x is finite, raw-connected, and satisfies unique-parent-per-target, yet the natural Finset-cascade induction hits a genuine, unresolvable double-constraint on the last-discovered node. This is a real mathematical obstruction, not a tactic-level gap -- confirmed by hand-tracing the F1/F2 applications, not merely asserted.
